reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Early/late unilateral and bilateral diffuser deprivation with recovery, cortical feature matching and optokinetic corroboration.

checks.reason: No explicit pre-execution consultation and transfer check of previous primary Methods, supplements or a validated technical protocol is proposed. Local pilots, welfare approval and promises to fill unknown settings do not meet this separate requirement.

Core exposure duration/intensity, stimulus timing and cortical acquisition/response settings remain a list to select later, without executable quantitative settings or a sufficiently specified calibration-to-setting procedure.

Optical/stimulus and response calibration is named, but quantitative acceptance-to-action thresholds or a concrete derivation of tolerances for eye isolation, delivered contrast and mapping reliability are absent.
Animal/cluster replication and pilot variability are recognized, but no quantitative power or interval-width target is linked to the meaningful effect and independent-unit variance.
Contrasts and clustering are recognized, but the actual response/distribution model, assumption diagnostics and specified multiplicity policy remain incomplete.
Age, exposure dose and stimulus-parameter exploration has no bounded candidate grid or objective range-selection/search-stop rule before locking.
No complete raw-animal/unit-to-output manifest with calibration records, exact analysis versions/settings and all exclusions/deviations is specified.

No sham device/procedure control or equivalent retinal/thalamic patterned-input physiology is specified. Fundus clarity and optokinetic behavior alone do not isolate cortical from upstream sensory changes.

checks.quote: mean absolute difference in preferred orientation
checks.reason: Orientation is 180-degree periodic, but the absolute-difference estimator is not circularly wrapped. Restricting matching to binocularly driven cells lacks a lost/weak-cell denominator rule, so selection can alter the mean.

checks.quote: tuning curves z-scored or normalized to peak/spontaneous
checks.reason: Positive scalar or affine within-curve normalization does not change the preferred-orientation argmax, and cannot by itself remove a difference in the main interocular preferred-orientation metric. The claimed gain-versus-structure discriminator needs an explicit noise/estimation model or independent gain manipulation.
No prospective equivalence/effect-precision rule supports this negative absence claim. Stating measurement limits is useful but not a replacement for that decision criterion.

Relevant experience/timing question, prospective welfare/model criteria and bounded two-age limitations. The specific gain-identification error is assessed at P09, not duplicated across general logic checks.

historical_match_reason: Developmental question, experience mechanism and unilateral manipulation match. The proposed main feature readout has a non-identifying normalization rule and lacks the sealed peripheral/upstream control for cortical interpretation; an experienced-eye redistribution is secondary and not adequately validated. No qualified joint match.
